facts.title: NetKV: Network-Aware Decode Instance Selection for Disaggregated LLM Inference
facts.event_hint: Shows that cache+load-aware PD-disaggregation schedulers are provably arbitrarily suboptimal as context grows once the network term is ignored, and gives a network-cost-oracle + O(|D|) greedy decode selector (NetKV) that fixes it.
facts.problem: Disaggregated LLM inference forces the KV cache to traverse the datacenter network before decoding, so transfer time enters the TTFT budget directly. Existing schedulers route on compute load and prefix-cache locality alone, ignoring topological distance and dynamic congestion between prefill and decode instances, which becomes arbitrarily suboptimal as context length grows.
facts.mechanism: Adds a thin operator-to-scheduler interface exposing a network cost oracle; proves that ignoring the network term makes cache-aware-only scheduling arbitrarily suboptimal as context length grows; NetKV is an O(|D|) per-request greedy decode-instance selector consuming that oracle, with tier rankings provably robust to stale telemetry. Requires no transport, inference-engine, or hardware changes.

evidence.claim: NetKV reduces mean TTFT by up to 21.2% over round-robin and 17.6% over a tuned cache+load-aware scheduler.
NetKV lifts SLO attainment by up to 20.1 percentage points.
evidence.value: up to 20.1 percentage points SLO attainment

evidence.claim: Time Between Tokens overhead stays below 0.5 ms in every condition tested.
Ignoring the network term renders cache-aware-only scheduling arbitrarily suboptimal as context length grows.

facts.evaluation_context: 64-GPU four-tier fat-tree simulator driven by Mooncake traces. Complexity: O(|D|) per request. No transport/engine/hardware changes. Absolute TTFT values and exact workload mix not in abstract.
facts.limitations: Abstract-level evidence only; results are simulation-based (not bare-metal), driven by Mooncake traces. Full paper body not fetched, so the form of the network cost oracle, stale-telemetry bounds, and hardware confirmation pending validation.
facts.project_relevance: Centrally relevant to the TPN inference-network track: it formalizes why KVCache cross-node transfer topology must enter the scheduler, and pairs naturally with byte-side reductions (SpectrumKV) and transfer-engine approaches (SmartGen, Mooncake). The operator-to-scheduler network-oracle interface is the kind of hook a DPU/SmartNIC could satisfy directly, and it is directly relevant to agent serving where growing context makes the network term dominant.
